summary: Yu Suzuki's 1986 Sega dirt-bike racing game, often viewed as the off-road counterpart to Hang-On, with arcade bike cabinets and home versions that diverge in content.

entries.title: Enduro Racer
entries.definitive_edition: Arcade for main route; Japanese Master System for extra levels

emulation.notes: Use MAME or original arcade hardware for primary; use a Master System emulator or Japanese hardware for the extra-level secondary route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Full arcade dirt-bike cabinet for primary; Japanese Master System content for completion

primary.version: Original Sega arcade release, preferably full dirt-bike cabinet
primary.why: Enduro Racer was built for Sega arcade hardware with stand-up handlebar and full-sized dirt-bike cabinet versions. The arcade release is the highest-fidelity and most authentic route, while the Japanese Master System release has extra unique levels that make it a secondary completion route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the arcade version in MAME/original hardware; use the full dirt-bike cabinet where available, then play the Japanese Master System version for its additional levels.

secondary.exclusive_content: Japanese cartridge has ten unique levels, while other territories have half the unique levels because of smaller cartridge size.
secondary.what_to_play: Play the Japanese Master System version after the arcade primary to see the extra level set.
secondary.why: Arcade is the fidelity route; the Japanese Master System version has sourced extra level content.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Sega arcade release with stand-up handlebar and full-sized dirt-bike cabinet versions.
all_releases.reason: primary: original and highest-fidelity cabinet route.

all_releases.fidelity: Japanese 256 KB Master System release with ten unique levels.
all_releases.reason: secondary: play for extra unique levels after the arcade primary.

all_releases.fidelity: Export Master System release with reduced unique level count due to smaller cartridge size.
all_releases.reason: skip: lower-fidelity than arcade and less complete than Japanese Master System.

all_releases.fidelity: Activision home-computer port with five tracks and two-player multiplayer.
all_releases.reason: skip: lower-fidelity home-computer route; multiplayer is a port feature but not the chosen secondary content over the Japanese Master System's larger level set.

all_releases.fidelity: Activision home-computer port with four levels built from harder versions of two base levels.
all_releases.reason: skip: lower-fidelity and less complete than arcade plus Japanese Master System secondary.
skip: lower-fidelity home-computer route and no sourced content advantage over arcade plus Japanese Master System secondary.

skip: lower-fidelity home-computer route and no sourced content advantage over arcade plus Japanese Master System secondary.

all_releases.fidelity: Virtual Console re-release in North America and Europe.
all_releases.reason: skip: official access route but no sourced content advantage over arcade plus Japanese Master System secondary.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Arcade is the cabinet-fidelity route; Japanese Master System has the larger sourced level set among home versions.

entries.remaster_caveats: Export Master System cartridges have fewer unique levels than the Japanese 256 KB release; Wii Virtual Console is an access route, not a remaster.
